articles.title: Giants, Vikings 'Most Aggressive' in RB Trade Talks, NFL Rumors Reveal amid Jonathan Taylor Buzz
articles.summary: As the trade market around the Indianapolis Colts and star running back Jonathan Taylor continues to swirl, keep an eye on the New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
As the trade market around the Indianapolis Colts and star running back Jonathan Taylor continues to swirl, keep an eye on the New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings.

According to Albert Breer of SI.com, the Colts have "let teams know they'll have to be blown away to trade" Taylor, but the "Giants and Vikings have been most aggressive in looking for running backs on the trade market the last couple weeks."

The Giants could use a more dynamic, home-run hitting option in the backfield to complement John Harbaugh's preferred way of playing. Taylor and Cam Skattebo would be quite the one-two punch, though whether the Giants are at the stage in their rebuild where they should be giving up draft assets for a 27-year-old running back is certainly debatable.

The Vikings, meanwhile, desperately need some more juice on the offensive side of the ball. Their 6-1 record to this point is largely down to a swarming defense and excellent special-teams unit, but Kyler Murray and the offense have struggled. Taylor would undoubtedly provide a spark.

But adding a three-time Pro Bowler in the backfield won't come cheap. Breer believes it will ultimately cost a team a Christian McCaffrey-esque return (second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks across two drafts). Whether the Giants or Ravens—or any other team around the NFL—is willing to take that plunge remains to be seen.

articles.title: QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 8
articles.summary: Week 8's quarterback performances were all over the board.
articles.body:
Week 8's quarterback performances were all over the board.

The Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow accomplished something that a quarterback hasn't done since Norm Van Brocklin in 1951. Conversely, Baker Mayfield didn't complete a single pass, yet the Tampa Bay Buccaneers still managed a double-digit victory. Somewhere between those two points, the Baltimore Ravens were forced to play their emergency quarterback due to injuries suffered by Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Oh, the Arizona Cardinals benched Jacoby Brissett as well.

These massive swings are exactly why Bleacher Report assesses every quarterback performance throughout the season to see how the position evolves through a campaign.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYJ | PHI | PIT | TB | TEN | WAS

Arizona Cardinals: Jacoby Brissett & Gardner Minshew II

Stat Line : Brissett, 10 of 23 for 119 yards and an interception; Minshew, 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns

Head coach Mike LaFleur finally made the call to move off Jacoby Brissett as the Arizona Cardinals' QB1. LaFleur benched Brissett, which allowed a little Minshew magic to occur.

Gardner Minshew took over the Cardinals' offense during Arizona's final third-quarter possession. From that point, Arizona scored four straight touchdowns to force overtime. The Cardinals needed two offensive series in overtime but eventually pulled off the upset.

Minshew has a history of providing a team with short-term juice. He's now done so for the Cardinals.

"He put on his cape and became Superman," head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters . Though Arizona must seriously consider how long Minshew will lead the way, because the organization eventually needs to see what rookie Carson Beck can do now that the door has been opened to change.

Score : 16-0 loss vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Stat Line : eight of 24 for 124 yards and four interceptions

Inexplicably, the Atlanta Falcons lost Sunday without the Tampa Bay Buccaneers completing a pass.

Penix completed a few passes. Maybe the Falcons should have reassessed their approach, because the downpour obviously affected quarterback play. Ultimately, the Falcons' signal-caller threw four interceptions.

Penix's counterpart, Baker Mayfield, may not have completed a pass, but he still finished the game with a higher quarterback rating. The Atlanta quarterback threw more passes than Mayfield attempted passes.

The conditions were what they were. The Bucs found a way. The Falcons failed to do so. Furthermore, Penix's decision-making should still be questioned based on where he decided to go with some of those passes.

"I've never thrown four picks in a game," Penix said afterward . "Man, I'm gonna shake back. I promise you that I will."

Baltimore Ravens: Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley & Joe Fagnano

Stat Line : Jackson, zero for one and zero passing yards; Huntley, two of four passing for zero yards; Fagnano, 10 of 21 passing for 91 yards and an interception

Emergency quarterbacks are rarely called upon to play in an NFL game. To the Baltimore Ravens' dismay, they were were forced to field three quarterbacks Saturday, with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano playing the majority of Sunday's contest against the Buffalo Bills.

Lamar Jackson's injury is the primary headline coming out of the action. Jackson, who just returned from another injury, smacked his throwing hand on a helmet during his first pass attempt and needed to leave the game. He'll now require surgery on his thumb, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . The Ravens will place Jackson on injured reserve and the two-time MVP's season may be done.

Then, Tyler Huntley suffered a turf toe injury, which forced Fagnano into the lineup.

"Everybody tried to speak up, but it's different when you lose not one, but two of your quarterbacks," wide receiver Zay Flowers told reporters . "It's difficult to try to do anything, because now you're on your third (quarterback), and your third is your last, and you never know what's going to happen after that."

Stat Line : 21 of 34 for 289 yards, two touchdowns and an interception; seven carries for 30 yards and a score

Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills don't lose after their bye week. Meanwhile, the team's quarterback is well on his way to becoming a two-time MVP if Allen continues to perform at the same level.

As Shawn Syed of Sumer Sports noted, the Bills currently own the league's top-ranked offense in EPA per play and Allen leads all quarterbacks in Total EPA.

Along the way, Allen surpassed Jim Kelly as the Bills' all-time leader in touchdown passes during Sunday's contest. Oh, Allen's nine rushing touchdowns lead the NFL as well. When Buffalo started its contest slowly against the Baltimore Ravens, Allen provided the spark that pushed the team toward 20 second-half points.

"I mean, look, with Josh, we're spoiled, right?" Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters . "He literally is one of one. He's incredible. And there's a lot of football still ahead of him."

Score : 27-19 loss vs. Green Bay Packers

Stat Line : 23 of 41 for 209 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Bryce Young was under duress throughout this past week's Thursday Night Game . The Green Bay Packers defense pressured Young on 22 of his dropbacks, according to ESPN's Mike Kaye . The Packers' six sacks matched Young's six completions when pressured.

Obviously, a quarterback can't thrive in that situation and Young hasn't. However, a quarterback can improve the situation to a degree, as Young did earlier this season but failed to do so as of late.

"I would say that it certainly doesn't look like he's got that quick, make-you-miss type of deal," Panthers coach Dave Canales said of his quarterback . "But he was able to create some space for himself. But the rush got after us and that's the bottom line. We've gotta take care of that first part of it, so we have an element of time to be able to execute the play."

Stat Line : 38 of 48 for 462 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions; four rushes for 10 yards and a score

The Cincinnati Bengals trailed 13-0 at the start of Sunday's second quarter. The Tennessee Titans were positioned to pull off one of the season's biggest upsets. Then, Joe Burrow turned on the switch.

Burrow led six scoring drives over the next four quarters. He threw five touchdowns and scampered for one more. In doing so, he became only the second quarterback in NFL history to threw for 450 or more yards and five touchdowns, while adding a rushing score, according to ESPN Insights .

The performance wasn't perfect. Far from it. Burrow also chucked three interceptions, which were poor decisions. However, he responded and led his team to a critical victory that keeps the Bengals half-a-game behind the Pittsburgh Steelers in the AFC North.

"The interceptions are so tough, and he'll want those throws back, but there were 40 other plays where he was playing at an elite level, and that's part of the game," Bengals left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. told reporters . "It's unfortunate that we turned the ball over, but you can't ask him to play perfect. It's tough. For him to go out there and fight and finish the way he did in that second half and in overtime, it was the reason we were able to win this game."

Cleveland Browns: Deshaun Watson & Shedeur Sanders

Score : 27-6 loss vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Stat Line : Watson, 27 of 39 for 324 yards and a fumble lost; Shedeur Sanders, two of two for two yards

Deshaun Watson's stat line looks impressive in a vacuum, though the Pittsburgh Steelers controlled the contest.

The Steelers set the tone early by pressuring Watson on 65 percent of his first-half dropbacks, according to ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi . In total, Pittsburgh sacked Watson eight times and registered 13 quarterback hits.

"We can't let the quarterback get touched that much," Browns guard Zion Johnson told reporters . "but like I just said, we got to own our own mistakes and fight like hell to fix it."

Watson hasn't been great this season, but he's been effective, especially late in contests. A quarterback can't do much when he's pressured like Watson was throughout this AFC North matchup. Plus, the Steelers did an excellent job keeping the Browns quarterback contained so he couldn't affect the game as a runner. In fact, Watson's two rushing yards were his fewest during any 2026 contest.

Score : 33-30 loss vs. Arizona Cardinals

Stat Line : 19 of 29 for 195 yards and a touchdown

The Dallas Cowboys defense has taken the brunt of the blame for this year's failures and deservedly so. However, Dallas' offense isn't entirely without blame.

After establishing a 24-10 fourth-quarter lead, the Cowboys failed to score a touchdown twice despite being inside Arizona's 30-yard line during subsequent drives, then failed to move the ball in overtime.

Dak Prescott's 195 passing yards were his second-fewest this season and his 61.2 QBR was the lowest. Obviously, Brian Schottenheimer's play-calling was too conservative down the stretch. At the same time, Schottenheimer should have the confidence to put the ball in his quarterback's hands during critical moments.

"It's all of us," Prescott told reporters . "Don't put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that's weak. I think that's cowardly. This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it, coaches and support staff. It's never just one person's fault.

Score : 28-24 win vs. Kansas City Chiefs

Stat Line : 20 of 32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns

Once again, Bo Nix excelled late in a contest and helped lead the Denver Broncos to victory. Head coach Sean Payton may prefer to start faster, but the end result is all that matters.

In the latest example, the Broncos trailed the rival Kansas City Chiefs by 11 points heading into Sunday's fourth quarter. Nix led two touchdown drives during the final frame to capture the victory.

During those two possessions, Nix complete five of six passes. Although running back Jonah Coleman deserves significant credit after taking a one-yard pass and turning it into a 51-yard scamper, which led to the game-deciding touchdown.

Overall, Nix has posted the league's best quarterback rating when trailing by one score in the fourth quarter since the start of the 1991 campaign, according to the Associated Press' Josh Dubow .

Stat Line : 18 of 25 for 176 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Jared Goff's interception-less streak ended Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings. Even when Goff finally threw an interception, he really didn't. The quarterback's intended target slipped coming out of his break and wasn't in the right spot for the pass. Stuff happens.

Otherwise, Goff remained his (mostly) efficient and calm self from the pocket, even playing against the game's most aggressive defense. Minnesota blitzed Goff on 89.7 percent of his dropbacks, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . The Lions' signal-caller completed 17 of his 18 passes when facing pressure. Goff also had the luxury of leaning on the team's run game. The Lions ran the ball 39 times in total. Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki combined for 218 yards on the ground, thus wearing down the Vikings defense and making life somewhat easier on the team's quarterback.

Stat Line : 30 of 41 for 288 yards, three touchdowns and an interception

The Green Bay Packers' offensive line is in upheaval. The team can't run the ball. Green Bay's wide receivers drop more passes than any other unit. Even the Packers' special teams have let the offense down when a drive doesn't end with a touchdown. Despite everything, Jordan Love has taken all of it in stride and played well.

"Can't say enough great things about him because he's carrying the burden of everything right now, just dealing the ball and throwing a lot of great passes," head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters .

Amazingly, Love is still pushing the ball down the field more than any other quarterback. As Steve Palazzolo of the CTM Show noted, the Packers' signal-caller has the highest percentage of games since the start of the 2020 season with at least 40 attempts and an average depth of target over 10 yards.

Indianapolis Colts: Daniel Jones & Anthony Richardson

Score : 42-7 loss vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : Jones, 19 of 28 for 144 yards, one touchdowns and two interceptions; Richardson, two of two for eight yards

After losing four straight games and trading two of the team's best players, the Indianapolis Colts' direction is obvious. The organization is already looking toward the future. A future that almost certainly won't include Daniel Jones based on his play. A change at quarterback could be coming sooner rather than later.

"I'm gonna evaluate everything," head coach Shane Steichen said when asked about Jones' standing as the Colts' QB1. "Every position going forward." Jones has been unable to recapture the magic of last season. Instead, he's thrown at least one interception in all but one game this year and a pair of picks in two of Indianapolis' last three contests. The Colts were flat out dominated Sunday. The team is clearly making moves to prepare for next offseason. The quarterback position must be evaluated. Anthony Richardson Sr. remains on the roster. Indianapolis might as well see what it has in the former fourth overall draft pick.

Stat Line : 10 of 14 for 210 yards, three touchdowns and a fumble lost

Trevor Lawrence didn't need to do a lot in a game where the Jacksonville Jaguars ran for as many yards as the quarterback threw. Though Lawrence deserves credit for his efficiency.

As ESPN Insights noted , Lawrence became the first quarterback since the 2015 campaign to throw three touchdowns despite fewer then 15 total pass attempts. The Jaguars had two weeks to prepare for a floundering Indianapolis Colts squad. Liam Coen's squad was ready for their opponent and Florida weather.

"We knew it was going to rain," Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten told reporters . "We knew we were going to run the ball, and we just went out and imposed our will."

Lawrence has now thrown two or more touchdown passes in five of Jacksonville's seven games, including seven during his last two outings.

Stat Line : 30 of 41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw a game-winning touchdowns...until he didn't. A false start on right tackle Jaylon Moore prevented the go-ahead score, and the Denver Broncos' Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes during the final play of the game.

The Chiefs have now lost two in a row. Mahomes and Co. haven't made the plays everyone has become accustomed to seeing from Kansas City's offense making during that stretch. The group isn't playing clean football, which has haunted the team.

"We had to go to a different play (on) that last one, and they covered it well," Mahomes told reporters . "Whenever you get there—you get that close—and you don't capitalize, you take that on yourself, and you learn from it."

Stat Line : 19 of 26 for 247 yards and three touchdowns

Kirk Cousins understands the assignment. It's his job to get the ball to the Las Vegas Raiders' best player, Brock Bowers.

"The coaching point with Brock has been like it was with [Vikings WR] Justin [Jefferson], when he's covered, you still need to throw it," Cousins told reporters after Sunday's victory over the New York Jets.

Good things happen when the two-time Pro Bowl tight end is featured. Cousins targeted Bowers 10 times, which led to 92 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

Truthfully, Bowers isn't a tight end. He's the Raiders' No. 1 wide receiver. He caught six passes Sunday aligned as an outside receiver, which is the most by a tight end over the last 10 years, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . Sometimes, the quarterback position can be as simple as, "Hey, I have an elite playmaker in my offense. Let's get him the ball."

Score : 24-9 loss vs. Los Angeles Chargers

Stat Line : 24 of 32 for 257 yards and two interceptions

Justin Herbert may not be completely broken but something within the Los Angeles Chargers offense is. The team's scheme under coordinator Mike McDaniel continues to be under fire.

"The way things are with the wide receivers and the running backs, fullbacks and the tight ends, it all ties together so it works," guard Cole Strange said after previous playing for McDaniel with the Miami Dolphins. "But everyone has to be on the same page and kind of like firing on all cylinders for it to really work. There's just a lot of moving pieces that can be tough for a whole building to figure out in a year."

At 0-7, patience is running thin. Maybe Herbert just isn't a good fit in the scheme. At the same time, he's playing tentatively and not making good decisions, with two more poor interceptions during Sunday's contest against the Los Angeles Rams.

Currently, Herbert ranks dead last among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per play, according to The Ringer's Sheil Kapadia .

Stat Line : 17 of 25 for 157 yards, a touchdown and an interception

The Los Angeles Rams have finally reached the point where the team is treading water with an opportunity to get back on track and possibly live up to preseason expectations. However, Sean McVay's squad still needs better play from the league's reigning MVP, Matthew Stafford.

Stafford and the Rams were fortunate they played the league's worst team this past Sunday. The Rams won comfortably over their Los Angeles counterpart, but the offense didn't play particularly well.

"We really couldn't have started any worse offensively," McVay told reporters . "As weird as things went in that first half, (Stafford) strings together an unbelievable two-minute drive to allow us to even have a lead, which was unreal based on how poorly we played."

Stafford isn't the same quarterback today as last season. That change tends to happen with aging signal-callers. Still, the 38-year-old has plenty left in the tank to provide peak performance for stretches. If the Rams can't rely on their quarterback to be as consistent, the squad should lean more heavily on its run game, as it has over the last two weeks.

Score : 24-19 loss vs. New England Patriots

Stat Line : 21 of 32 for 211 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

The Miami Dolphins have been far more competitive in recent weeks, but something still seems to be missing.

Against the Cincinnati Bengals and the New York Jets—the latter of which turned into the Dolphins' first win—Malik Willis carried the ball 16 times for a combined 111 yards. During Miami's losses to the Minnesota Vikings and New England Patriots, Willis ran the ball three times for 13 yards. The Dolphins don't feature significant offensive firepower. The quarterback's ability to scramble or contribute on designed runs must be a bigger part of the offense. He's a potential playmaker, who gets bottled up too often. Miami's coaching staff should make his athleticism a staple of their offense to provide a regular dynamic opposing defenses must be prepared to address. To Willis' credit, he completed over 65 percent of his passes during back-to-back outings for the first time this season. Still, the Dolphins came up short during the second half against their AFC East rival.

Stat Line : 17 of 29 for 210 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

The Minnesota Vikings finally came across an opponent with an offense good enough in the Detroit Lions to test Brian Flores' defense. Meanwhile, the Vikings' offense can't seem to get out of the starting blocks, which led to the team's first loss of the season.

Minnesota's quarterbacks have yet to surpass 250 passing yards in any game, including 210 Sunday from Kyler Murray despite playing against the league's worst defense. The growing frustration within the unit is becoming visible during games, specifically from All-Pro wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who has now produced fewer than 45 receiving yards in three of the Vikings' last four games.

"We gotta find ways to get him the ball," Murray told reporters . "Obviously they're gonna double him, and they did today… this is my first year with him… Obviously he's frustrated, and that's understandable. He is who he is, and he has every right to feel the way he feels when he doesn't get the ball."

Stat Line : 16 of 20 for 199 yards and two touchdowns

The term "franchise quarterback" is subjective yet often ubiquitous in its designation. A true franchise quarterback is capable of elevating his team, especially the play of those around him.

Case in point, the New England Patriots' offense was slammed by injuries as the unit entered Sunday's matchup against the Miami Dolphins. AJ Brown, Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins weren't in the lineup. The team was starting two backup guards. Tight end Hunter Henry also left the contest due to an injured foot.

Somehow, Maye still played an efficient game and helped lead his team to a victory.

"You want to be a great quarterback in the National Football League, there's not a whole lot of excuses—you go out there and find ways to win for the football team," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters . "I know that's who he is and who he wants to continue to be. He throws to the open guy and controls our offense and gets guys in the right spot."

Score : 38-33 loss vs. Las Vegas Raiders

Stat Line : 20 of 32 for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Statistically, this current version of Geno Smith is the best quarterback New York Jets history. Please, stop the snickering after reading the previous sentence. Others probably rolled their eyes. Yes, Smith has been better than expected but the best ever?

As Football Perspective noted , Smith's current passer rating (104.5) through the first half of the 2026 campaign is higher than any Jets quarterback has produced in any single season. Meanwhile, the Jets are actually wasting solid-to-good quarterback play. New York held a 30-21 third-quarter lead. Las Vegas scored 17 points during the final 20 minutes of regulation play. To be fair, the Jets offense sputtered down the stretch Sunday and wasn't particularly good in the red zone. But Smith and Co. did more than enough to win the game, which still didn't happen.

Score : 27-10 loss vs. Washington Commanders

Stat Line : 23 of 34 for 212 yards, an interception and a fumble lost; four carries for 25 yards

The Philadelphia Eagles haven't been in sync since Tanner McKee became the starting quarterback in Week 6. As Jeff Kerr noted , the Eagles rank 26th or worse in points per game, yards per play (dead last), passer rating, yards per attempt, yards per game and points per possession since that point.

To be fair, the Eagles offense wasn't exactly on fire with Jalen Hurts as its starting quarterback. Still, the unit has taken another step back and barely resembles an NFL offense at this juncture.

"I've been in situations like this before," running back Saquon Barkley told reporters . "We're grinding. We're trying to best to do our little things. We're getting coached great. I can't sit here and lie. Our coaches are doing a really good job, I feel like. Even if we're falling apart, you know, Nick is doing a really good job of just stepping up, calling us out. We're having great weeks of practices. It's just not translating to the game."

Stat Line : 13 of 25 for 172 yards and an interception

Aaron Rodgers simultaneously understands the Pittsburgh Steelers sit atop the AFC North standings after Sunday's victory over the Cleveland Browns and his offense's performance simply isn't good enough.

"Not very complete," Rodgers told reporters . "Defense played excellent. Special teams did fine. But offense should've been a lot more points." The group isn't executing at a high level, specifically in the passing game. Rodgers isn't entirely at fault, of course. DK Metcalf has three or fewer catches in his three of his last four outings. His downfield bobble led to Rodgers' interception during this latest contest. Despite a relatively one-sided victory, the Steelers offense still has significant concerns regarding the ability to push the ball down the field with any consistency and red-zone efficiency or lack thereof.

Stat Line : no completions on three pass attempts; four carries for 14 yards

Last week, Baker Mayfield joked about how well he handed the ball off to Bucky Irving. His greatness at handoffs was on full display Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons.

Due to a torrential downpour, Mayfield didn't complete a single pass. Though he only attempted three. In doing so, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a pass.

To take Tampa's recent performances one sept further, Mayfield threw for 64 combined yards over the last two weeks and the Bucs still won by double-digits in both contests, which is the fewest passing yardage with that margin of victory since the 1942 Pittsburgh Steelers, per Trey Wingo .

"I'll do whatever it takes to win," Mayfield told reporters . "That's all that matters to me." Meanwhile, Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell combined for 310 rushing yards Sunday. The best thing Mayfield did was fumble three times then recover all three. But, hey, a win is a win.

Score : 43-36 loss vs. Cincinnati Bengals

Stat Line : 26 of 40 for 304 yards, two touchdowns and a fumble lost; seven carries for 41 yards

Cam Ward played his best game as a professional quarterback Sunday. It wasn't enough to elevate the Tennessee Titans over the Cincinnati Bengals, not with Joe Burrow on the other sideline. Ward's 304 passing yards set a new career-high. Ward led the Titans offense on back-to-back touchdown drives when trailing during the fourth quarter. His playmaking was present and his decision-making improved compared to previous outings.

The Titans still lost in overtime, but hope has been rekindled after a disappointing start of the season from the 2025 No. 1 overall draft pick. Granted, Ward can't take a sack that stalled Tennessee's final offensive possession in regulation. Still, he had his team in a position to win and the defense let the Titans downs.

Score : 27-10 win vs. Philadelphia Eagles

Stat Line : 16 of 29 for 217 yards and a touchdowns; two carries for 23 yards

Jayden Daniels is playing mostly clean football, but his team isn't.

The Washington Commanders committed nine penalties for 70 yards Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles. The issue is particularly bad regarding presnap penalties.

"Coaches could beat a dead horse all they want," Daniels told reporters . "At the end of the day, you got to take accountability. You got to focus. You can't have mental lapses. Ultimately, that's on us."

The quarterback added, "It was very frustrating. But I think the message is, just, everybody—and the 'PG way' is—'Lock in. Focus. Take a deep breath and overcommunicate. Like, it doesn't matter if they know the snap count or what we're doing. Overcommunicate. Make sure everybody knows, so we don't have those mental lapses.'"

Washington has experienced its fair share of communication problems this season, whether it's presnap or in critical moments.

Still, Daniels was able to lead his team to its second victory against a depleted opponent. How the Commanders respond against the Los Angeles Rams this coming weekend will be a much better indication of where the quarterback and his team currently stand.

articles.title: Deion Sanders enjoys Colorado’s field storming, but girlfriend Karrueche Tran has one urgent mission after Kansas State win
articles.summary: Deion Sanders’ girlfriend, Karrueche Tran, appeared worried when Colorado fans rushed onto the field following the Buffaloes’ 27-24 overtime win against
articles.body: Deion Sanders’ girlfriend, Karrueche Tran, appeared worried when Colorado fans rushed onto the field following the Buffaloes’ 27-24 overtime win against Kansas State on October 31. A video shared on November 1 showed Tran quickly gathering her belongings before heading towards Sanders. “I better get to my man,” she told her friend, explaining why she wanted to reach him amid the celebrations at Folsom Field.Karrueche Tran rushes towards Deion Sanders during Colorado field stormThe video showed Tran watching the celebrations from the stands as Colorado fans flooded the field after their dramatic win. As she noticed the crowd moving towards the playing area, she began collecting her things and preparing to leave her seat.Her friend, who was recording the moment, appeared to have trouble hearing what Tran was saying and asked her to repeat herself. Tran then made her reason clear, saying, “I better get to my man.”Her reaction suggested that she wanted to reach Sanders and make sure he was safe while hundreds of excited supporters celebrated around him. The Halloween game also meant many fans were wearing costumes as they made their way onto the field.The celebration followed a difficult run for Colorado, which had lost five straight games before facing Kansas State. For Tran, however, the focus appeared to be on Sanders rather than the result. While the head coach was enjoying the victory with his players and supporters, his girlfriend was keen to get closer to him as the crowd took over the field.Deion Sanders reacts to Colorado fans storming the field after Kansas State winThe Buffaloes’ victory was far from easy. Colorado looked close to securing the game in regulation, but Kansas State quarterback Blake Barnett connected with Garrett Oakley for a touchdown with just two seconds remaining. That made it 21-21 and sent the contest into overtime.Kansas State managed a field goal in the extra period, giving the Wildcats a 24-21 lead. Colorado then had its chance, and quarterback Isaac Wilson found tight end Charlie Williams with an 11-yard touchdown pass to finish the game at 27-24.Running back Richard Young also played a major role in the win. He carried the ball 24 times for 120 yards and scored twice, including a 22-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. It was the best rushing performance of his college career. Colorado finished with 222 rushing yards, its highest total of the season.Sanders was clearly happy with the way the fans supported his team after the final whistle. Speaking about the crowd, he said, “We got the victory. Young men are happy. Staff is happy. The fan base is happy. God bless the fan base. Still showed up. Still cheered their butt off. Still supported. Still was energetic.”He also made it clear that he had no problem with supporters entering the field to celebrate.“I love it. I want to see the kids rush the field. I absolutely love it,” Sanders said.However, the celebration could bring a financial penalty for Colorado. The Big 12 has previously issued fines of $50,000 for field-storming incidents, although no punishment had been announced for this particular game at the time of the reports.Sanders questioned the rule when discussing the possible fine, saying, “How is it $50,000 for rushing the field? Who made that a rule? That isn’t right.”The win improved Colorado’s overall record to 3-5 and gave Sanders his first Big 12 victory of the 2026 season. The Buffaloes still have four games left and need three more wins to become eligible for a bowl game. Despite their difficult season, the victory gave the team and its supporters a much-needed reason to celebrate.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
After the Denver Broncos held on for a 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, quarterback Bo Nix revealed to star signal-caller Patrick Mahomes that he feared his late-game heroics.

"I've always admired you. Watching you play, you do a great job. I was scared to death when you got the ball back," Nix admitted.

After the Broncos took the lead with less than two minutes left in the fourth quarter, the Chiefs had the chance for a game-winning drive, but Denver's goal-line stand preserved the win for Nix and company.

The Broncos and Chiefs have now split the regular-season series 1-1, so any chance of revenge for Mahomes will have to come in the playoffs.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson 'Balked' at Ravens' Contract Negotiations, New NFL Rumors Reveal After Injury
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson's future—both for this season, after he suffered a thumb injury on Sunday that will require surgery and a stint on injured reserve, and beyond—is very much in question.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson's future—both for this season, after he suffered a thumb injury on Sunday that will require surgery and a stint on injured reserve, and beyond—is very much in question.

According to Albert Breer of SI.com, "My understanding has been that the Ravens wanted to negotiate a long-term extension with Jackson after [new head coach Jesse Minter] got the job. Jackson balked. He also has a no-tag clause in his contract. So if he wants to hit the market as an unfettered free agent in 2028, all he really has do is... nothing. If he plays it out, and wants to get to the market, health-permitting, he can. In that scenario, would he look to go home to Miami? It's a ways off, and I'd expect the Ravens to make a real effort to get him locked up. But again, he holds a lot of the cards here."

Jackson, 29, has appeared in just five games this season and only played in one snap during Sunday's 36-10 loss against the Buffalo Bills. He also missed four games last season. Since 2021, he's missed four games or more in a season on four separate occasions, and the 2026 campaign is shaping up to be the fewest games he's ever played in a season during his career.

And the 2027 season is complicated. As Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic noted, because Jackson and the Ravens didn't come to terms on a contract extension in the offseason, "the team restructured his contract instead. As a result, his cap number rises to $84-plus million in 2027, a bloated figure that would make it untenable for [general manager Eric DeCosta] and the front office to construct the rest of the roster."

That would be alleviated with an offseason extension, but Jackson has already seemingly balked at signing one and now the Ravens have to take his injury history into account. It will certainly be a storyline to track in Baltimore over the next year.

articles.title: Eagles Trade Options Teased by NFL Insider amid Saquon Barkley Rumors Ahead of 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles could still be a seller ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline while holding onto their biggest trade chip.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles could still be a seller ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline while holding onto their biggest trade chip.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that star running back Saquon Barkley will finish out the year in Philly. Rapoport followed up Monday to say other vets such as cornerback Riq Woolen and guard Landon Dickerson could be dangled in deals:

The Eagles' 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders was their sixth in a row. They're last in the NFC East and a half-game behind the New Orleans Saints for the conference's worst record (2-6).

Philly should have enough talent to compete in 2027, though, so a full rebuild is off the table. Barkley, for example, will occupy a key role in the backfield next year.

That doesn't take outgoing trades off the table entirely. Woolen only signed a one-year contract, so flipping him for a draft pick would be better than letting him walk as a free agent for nothing. Dickerson is under contract through 2028, but his exit would clean up the payroll a bit when he's earning $19.5 million annually.

Rapoport didn't mention tight end Dallas Goedert or wide receiver Hollywood Brown, but both are in the impending free agent boat with Woolen.

Given the direction of the Eagles' fortunes, a trade or two feels inevitable in the coming days. Assuming that happens, don't expect to see a blockbuster.

articles.title: Aaron Glenn, Dan Quinn Hot Seats Updated by NFL Insider After Jets' Loss, Commanders' Win
articles.summary: There are a number of teams around the NFL who likely have head coaches on the hot seat at the moment. It wouldn't be surprising if the New York Jets (2-6) and Washington Commanders (2-4-1) were among them.
articles.body:
There are a number of teams around the NFL who likely have head coaches on the hot seat at the moment. It wouldn't be surprising if the New York Jets (2-6) and Washington Commanders (2-4-1) were among them.

But following Sunday's results—the Jets lost 38-33 against the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Commanders walloped the Eagles, 27-10—those seats may be diverging in temperature.

As Albert Breer of SI.com wrote, "The clock seems to be ticking on Jets coach Aaron Glenn now. Conversely, Commanders coach Dan Quinn has been able to settle some choppy waters."

There is some important context to consider here. The Jets have basically no chance of winning the AFC East at this point with the Buffalo Bills (6-1) and New England Patriots (5-3) nestled in at the top, and they would have to leapfrog seven teams to earn a Wild Card bid. For all intents and purposes, their season is already sunk barring a miraculous turnaround.

The Commanders, on the other hand, are just two games back of the New York Giants (4-2-1) in the mediocre NFC East. While a Wild Card berth is almost certainly out of the question—like the Jets, they would need to leapfrog seven teams to pull that off—winning the division is actually feasible.

The Commanders will need to start consistently winning games, of course. But there is hope in Washington, and while that hope remains, it may be enough to keep Quinn off the hot seat.

articles.title: Charlie Smyth: New Orleans Saints to evaluate kicker situation
articles.summary: Head coach Kellen Moore says the New Orleans Saints will "evaluate" kickers Dan Carlson and Charlie Smyth ahead of Sunday's game with the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Head coach Kellen Moore says the New Orleans Saints will "evaluate" kickers Daniel Carlson and Charlie Smyth ahead of Sunday's game with the Cleveland Browns.

Carlson has been the Saints' first-choice kicker this season, but the 31-year-old has struggled for consistency.

Smyth, a former Gaelic footballer from Mayobridge in County Down, made his NFL debut last season but returned to the practice roster after the Saints elected to bring in Carlson for the start of the current campaign.

However, Carlson's form has opened the door for Smyth to potentially return to the playing roster. Moore said both he and his coaching staff will "evaluate the field goal situation and opportunities".

Moore said that the Saints had not brought any additional kickers into their squad, which leaves Smyth and Carlson in contention to start against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

"That's something we'll have to work through and discuss to find the best solution for Sunday," said Moore.

"We'll see how it goes. We'll have some kicking sessions throughout this week and we'll see where we are at."

Former Gaelic footballer Smyth made 12 of 16 field goals and was successful on each of his 13 extra point attempts as a starter last season, after his historic NFL debut last November.

He had a mixed pre-season and Carlson was selected to be the Saints' first choice after a kicking competition ahead of the NFL season.

But Carlson has a success rate of 66% this season from 12 field goal attempts and his only perfect game with the boot came in September, when he landed three kicks against the Baltimore Ravens.

He has made 16 of his 18 extra point attempts as the Saints have just two wins from seven games this season.

articles.title: B/R Experts Week 9 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: We're eight weeks into the 2026 NFL regular season. And as is so often the case, things have gone like exactly no one expected.
articles.body:
We're eight weeks into the 2026 NFL regular season. And as is so often the case, things have gone like exactly no one expected.

Granted, some things have followed the script. We thought that the Buffalo Bills would be formidable—and they are. We thought that the Tennessee Titans would be a bad team—and they are.

However, there have been surprises galore. The Minnesota Vikings were the last team to suffer a loss, and they sit atop an NFC North where all four teams sport a winning record. After back-to-back 11-win seasons, the Los Angeles Chargers are still searching for win No. 1 on the season after another listless performance against the Rams.

The NFL landscape is constantly shifting—often in unexpected ways. And as they do every week, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have come together to try to make sense of it all, by ranking all 32 teams from worst to first.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYG | NO | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

Week 8 Result: Lost at Los Angeles Rams 24-9

The Los Angeles Chargers have been hard to watch for two months. They're the league's lowest-scoring team, and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's unit hasn't improved.

Coming off a Week 7 bye, the Chargers didn't score a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams and turned the ball over twice.

Los Angeles is stuck at the bottom of the power rankings, with an offense sinking into futility . -- Moton

Week 8 Result: Lost at Jacksonville 42-7

At this point, the Indianapolis Colts have only two things they can accomplish through the rest of the 2026 campaign.

First, they can trade as many pieces as possible before the league's deadline on Nov. 10 to build a war chest of draft assets going into the '27 offseason. Second, Anthony Richardson needs to be placed in the lineup and see if his career can be salvaged.

Somewhere along the way, head coach Shane Steichen will likely be relieved of his duties--whether the decision occurs during the regular season or happens directly afterward--and the Colts will eventually move past quarterback Daniel Jones.

Indianapolis is readying itself for a full-blown rebuild, which has been needed for quite some time. -- Sobleski

Week 8 Result: Lost at Cincinnati 43-36 (OT)

Moral victories don't exist in a bottom-line business like the NFL. However, the Tennessee Titans can look at their performance Sunday, specifically the play of quarterback Cam Ward, and be more encouraged today than they were entering their contest with the Cincinnati Bengals.

Ward provided his best professional game to date. The 2025 No. 1 overall draft pick posted his first 300-yard effort and responded with back-to-back touchdown drives after the Bengals established fourth-quarter leads.

Ultimately, Tennessee's defense, beyond safety Amani Hooker, did little to slow the Bengals' potent offense. Joe Burrow became only the second player in NFL history with 450 passing yards, five passing touchdowns and a rushing score in a game. Even so, Ward did more than enough to lead his team to victory. Tennessee's defense failed in this instance. -- Sobleski

Week 8 Result: Lost vs. New England 24-19

There are no moral victories in the NFL. And given that the Dolphins held a 13-3 lead over the Patriots at halftime Sunday, the team no doubt feels like this one got away from them.

But given how these Dolphins looked earlier in the season, there is progress being made in Miami—even if it's only incremental.

Perhaps most importantly for the Dolphins, after a rough start to his first season with the Dolphins, Malik Willis has looked better the last few weeks—he threw for 211 yards and two scores against the Pats and posted a passer rating north of 90.

In some respects, this may be the best-case for the Dolphins. Show some fight. Give young players a chance to impress. And keep stacking losses.

Because if Miami believes in Willis, bringing wide receiver Jeremiah Smith back to Florida wouldn't be the worst way to start the 2027 NFL Draft. – Davenport

The good news is that the New Orleans Saints didn't lose for the fifth time in six games in Week 8.

The bad news is that it was the Saints' bye.

The Saints have multiple issues. With Travis Etienne on injured reserve, New Orleans can't run the ball. The defense ranks in the bottom-five in both yards and points allowed per game.

And while speaking at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club , team owner Gayle Benson sounded like a woman whose patience was wearing thin.

"Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," she said. "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. Our players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable."

If many more losses pile up, big changes could be coming in The Big Easy. -- Davenport

Mathematically, the Eagles aren't out of the NFC East race yet. However, it certainly feels like it's time for Philly to start preparing for the future.

Jalen Hurts isn't coming back this season, and injuries have eroded the Eagles' skill group. Both the defense and the offensive line are shells of what they were during the 2024 championship run. After consecutive blowout losses to divisional foes, Philadelphia sits at 2-6 with little hope of righting the proverbial ship.

The big question now is whether Howie Roseman will consider parting out the roster at the trade deadline. -- Knox

Last week the New York Jets handed the previously winless Miami Dolphins their first victory of 2026. Somehow, what happened at Met Life Stadium in Week 8 might be worse.

The Jets out-gained the Raiders by over 100 yards and completely dominated the first half, only to see the defense fall apart after halftime. It was the team's fifth one-score loss of the season, and after the game head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that the team's inability to seal the deal is frustrating.

"I'm upset in general because of where we're at as a team -- and I mean that, for the record -- because there's always things that you're going to be things that you want to get better at," Glenn said. "So, if anything, if I want to put my thumb on something, that's it -- the record that we have right now."

With the Chiefs and Bills next up on the schedule, the Jets are barreling toward another miserable season.

And Glenn's days as head coach are probably numbered. – Davenport

Week 8 Result: Won vs. Philadelphia 27-10

The Washington Commanders got out of the NFC East basement with Sunday night's win over the Philadelphia Eagles. At 2-4-1, the Commanders still have a lot of ground to make up. However, they've found reasons for hope over the last few weeks.

Despite losing receiver Terry McLaurin to a season-ending injury in Week 6, Washington seemed to find some fight in its close loss to the San Francisco 49ers. They regained that intensity after a slow start on Sunday and rattled off 27 unanswered points to get win No. 2.

Washington can now think about climbing back into the playoff picture, but it'll need to start stacking complete performances like Sunday's. Next week will bring a good test, as the Commanders will host a talented, if underachieving, Los Angeles Rams team. -- Knox

The Arizona Cardinals needed a little Minshew magic to manage an impressive overtime victory over the Dallas Cowboys. The Cardinals trailed 17-3 in the third quarter when head coach Mike LaFleur decided to bench Jacoby Brissett and play Gardner Minshew II.

Minshew led Arizona to four straight second-half touchdowns before the Cardinals captured the win during extra time. Minshew's latest outing is a perfect example of what he does. The journeyman signal-caller can provide a short-term spark. But he's not the long-term answer.

Maybe the Cardinals see what Minshew can do for a few weeks. Whatever the case may be, Arizona must eventually evaluate third-round rookie Carson Beck before going into the offseason. -- Sobleski

In Week 7, the Falcons posted their most impressive win of the season to date, knocking off the undefeated San Francisco 49ers.

In Week 8, Atlanta flushed every bit of momentum the team built in that victory.

Granted, the weather conditions in the game didn't do the team any favors. But Falcons quarterback Michael Penix had one of the worst games of his career—a third of the passes he completed were to players for the Buccaneers.

As ugly as the loss was, it's not the end of the world—the Falcons play in a division that seemingly no one wants to win. But the Falcons are entering a brutal stretch on the schedule that includes five straight games against teams with winning records.

If Sunday's performance was any indication, by the end of that stretch Atlanta will be closer to a goose than a Falcon.

Week 8 Result: Lost vs. Arizona 33-30 (OT)

Halloween was on Saturday, which is fitting because the Dallas Cowboys stopped masquerading as a playoff contender in the middle of Sunday's home loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

Dallas had a 14-point lead in the third quarter and again in the fourth. However, its defense, which is again one of the worst in the NFL, had no answers after Arizona made a quarterback change. The Cardinals scored touchdowns while the Cowboys settled for field goals down the stretch, and the result was a demoralizing overtime loss at home.

Franchise owner Jerry Jones told reporters after the game that he won't make a coaching change during the season. If something significant doesn't change soon, though, Jones will be evaluating a third straight losing season. -- Knox

After a 1-5 start, the return of quarterback Baker Mayfield has spurred back-to-back wins for the Buccaneers. The thing is though, Mayfield had next to nothing to do with either of them.

Since Mayfield returned, he has completed seven passes. Total. None of them came in Week 8—for the first time since 1974, a team played an entire game without completing a pass.

Mayfield told reporters he's fine with winning any way he can.

"I'll do whatever it takes to win," Mayfield said. "That's all that matters to me."

In the win over Atlanta the Buccaneers ran for a franchise-record 324 yards, and the team has amassed a staggering 600 yards on the ground. But with two high-octane offensive teams next up in the Bears and Lions, Tampa is going to need a more balanced offense to keep the winning streak going. -- Davenport

General manager Nick Caserio was blunt in his assessment of the Houston Texans' defense after disappointing through the team's first seven games. Houston's offense has played relatively well, but the defense underperformed after finishing as last year's top-ranked unit.

"We're the worst team in the league in tackling," Caserio said . "Too many missed tackles. Giving up too many explosive plays. Take those two areas right there. If we tackle better and we give up less explosive plays, then (you'll) probably see a better result defensively."

Expect those previous problem areas to be points of emphasis coming out of the Texans' bye week, especially with the winless Los Angeles Chargers next on the docket. -- Sobleski

The Baltimore Ravens suddenly feel like a team that could be selling at the trade deadline and looking to prepare for next season. Baltimore's defense has shown some growth under new head coach Jesse Minter, but it hasn't been enough to consistently win games without Lamar Jackson.

Unfortunately, Jackson's return from an ankle injury lasted a single play, during which he suffered a thumb injury that will land him on injured reserve. It's unclear when or if Jackson will be back this season, and to make matters worse, backup Tyler Huntley was also injured on Sunday.

Baltimore currently sits in the AFC North basement, and with a Thursday matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars looming, it could be staring down a 4-5 record. -- Knox

The bloom is coming off the rose with Panthers quarterback Bryce Young.

After pacing the NFL in passing yards over the season's first month, Young has struggled the last couple of times out. Thursday night in Green Bay, Young averaged just 5.1 yards per attempt, threw a pick and was sacked half a dozen times.

While speaking to the media , Young said he's aware both he and the team need to level up.

"They executed better," Young said. "A lot of stuff was on film, but they just do a really good job of disguising. They're a really good defense. So, we have a lot of respect for them. They were better than us today, for sure. They deserve that win. We should have been better. We've just got to execute better -- that's all it is."

Carolina is still in first place in the NFC South. But which each passing week, first place in that division means less and less. -- Davenport

Week 8 Result: Won at New York Jets 38-33

The Las Vegas Raiders were well prepared for their second trip to the East Coast this season. They fell behind early, but Kirk Cousins showed why he still gives the Silver and Black the best chance to win, throwing for 247 yards and three touchdowns and scoring a touchdown on a quarterback sneak.

For now, head coach Klint Kubiak is trying to stay in the playoff picture , so expect Cousins to keep the starting job for the foreseeable future. Rookie first-rounder Fernando Mendoza's time will come, but the .500 Raiders should keep riding Cousins' arm for now.

The Raiders are a flawed team with an inefficient ground attack, averaging three yards per carry, and a leaky defense, but Cousins and the passing game gives them a chance to pull off victories. -- Moton

A few days after Jared Verse decided to open his mouth about the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Cleveland Browns got punched in the mouth by their AFC North rivals.

Cleveland got outplayed, outcoached, and out-physicaled by the Steelers on Sunday while continuing a couple of alarming trends. The Browns fell behind early, again, and they committed more penalties (nine) than any playoff hopeful should.

Considering how uncompetitive the Browns have looked in blowout losses to the Steelers and Jacksonville Jaguars, it's fair to wonder if they actually are a playoff-caliber team. It would be easier to take Cleveland seriously if it had at least one convincing victory on its resume. -- Knox

The New York Giants may have lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season, but they're not going away. New York turned to trade acquisition J.J. McCarthy at quarterback two weeks ago and won an overtime thriller against the Houston Texans.

New head coach John Harbaugh has the Giants on an upward trajectory, and his fingerprints are all over this team. He effectively benched Cam Skattebo to send a message in Week 6 and got a masterful performance from the second-year running back in the win over Houston. New York's defense has been quite efficient against the pass, and the Giants are playing great complementary football overall.

This certainly feels like a team that can keep stacking wins, provided McCarthy doesn't fall back into the bad habits he exhibited early in his career. At 4-2-1, the Giants managed to stay atop the NFC East despite being off in Week 8. -- Knox

Week 8 Result: Won vs. Los Angeles Chargers 24-9

At 4-4 after back-to-back wins, the presumptive Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams are finally in a position where a run should be possible.

Prior to the team's Week 11 bye, the Rams face the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals. Both are winnable matchups, even if Los Angeles fell to the Cardinals just two weeks ago.

Plus, help should be on the way. The NFL's reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, could play as early as this coming weekend. Though another week or two may be a more realistic possibility.

The Rams haven't fielded their intended at any point of this season. But Garrett's return should definitely provide a jolt when Los Angeles needs it the most and revive the squad's previous expectations. -- Sobleski

Jordan Love had to carry the Green Packers offense with his arm while running back Josh Jacobs was on the commissioner's exempt list.

In Jacobs' first two games back, Green Bay's ground attack has still been inefficient, averaging 2.8 yards per carry, but the defense is coming along under coordinator Jonathan Gannon, giving up an average of 19.5 points over the last two weeks.

With star edge-rusher Micah Parsons nearing a return from a torn ACL, the Packers defense could take pressure off Love and the passing attack by limiting opponents' scoring opportunities.

The Packers are on the rise after a 1-2 start. -- Moton

After coming up short in Chicago last week, the Patriots badly needed to get back on track in Week 8 lest they fall too far behind the AFC East-leading Buffalo Bills.

The Pats didn't exactly pile up the style points in Miami, but thanks to an efficient game from quarterback Drake Maye and five sacks from the defense, New England got back on track and kept pace with the Bills.

While addressing the media after the win, head coach Mike Vrabel lauded the play of Maye, who has rebounded nicely after a rocky start to the season.

"(If) you want to be a great quarterback in the National Football League, there's not a whole lot of excuses," Vrabel said. "You go out there and find ways to win for your football team. That's who he is and that's what he wants to continue to be."

The Patriots will need big games out of Maye that much more the next couple of weeks—matchups with a pair of NFC contenders in the Packers and Lions are next up before a Week 11 bye. – Davenport

Week 8 Result: Won vs. Tennessee 43-36 (OT)

The bad news is that the Cincinnati Bengals' defense hasn't improved as much as many expected it would during the offseason. Even without standout rookie receiver Carnell Tate, the Titans racked up 36 points and took the Bengals to overtime on Sunday.

The good news is that Cincinnati's offense seems to have flipped a switch since entering halftime of Week 7 in a 13-0 hole.

Over their past six quarters, Joe Burrow and the Bengals' offense have looked like Super Bowl material. The defense will have to play with more efficiency and more consistency for Cincinnati to actually make a run at Super Bowl LXI. However, Cincinnati has a legitimate chance to win the AFC North this season. -- Knox

On a four-game winning streak, the Steelers are on top of the AFC North and looking like a team that could actually go deep in the playoffs.

Pittsburgh's defense has rounded into form, and its rushing attack has started to take off in recent weeks. The offensive line is imposing its will on opposing defenses, while Aaron Rodgers is largely putting the offense in position to be successful.

The Steelers haven't been great at attacking defenses deep, but if they can bolster their receiver corps at the trade deadline, they could have a complete roster capable of challenging the AFC's top contenders. -- Knox

The Detroit Lions will get a much-deserved boost in the power rankings following a win over the Minnesota Vikings, the NFL's last undefeated team.

Also, credit the Lions' defense. Detroit has held its previous two opponents to 17 points or fewer. This team doesn't need to win a scoring shootout; it can grind out victories as well, which is a key characteristic of an elite-level squad.

Currently 2-0 within their division, the Lions are making a strong case as the best team in the NFC North. -- Moton

The Seattle Seahawks are the reigning Super Bowl champions. But they also haven't been an easy team to get a bead on. At their best, the defense is stifling and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is unstoppable. At their worst, the offense becomes one-dimensional and Sam Darnold starts seeing ghosts.

When last we saw the Seahawks though, it was the former—and with both Zach Charbonnet and rookie Jadarian Price set to return soon the offensive balance that has lacked at times should get a major boost.

Calling Darnold a game manager is unfair—he won a Super Bowl last year. But when he can play within himself, Seattle is the toughest of outs—especially at home. -- Sobleski

The Kansas City Chiefs have some defensive question marks after consecutive losses. They didn't have two of their top three cornerbacks in the previous outing. The club placed L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve and ruled out rookie first-rounder Mansoor Delane.

Against the Chiefs, quarterback Bo Nix had one of his most efficient outings of the season, completing 62.5 percent of his passes and throwing for 222 yards and two touchdowns. He didn't light up Kansas City's depleted secondary, but the Chiefs allowed touchdowns on back-to-back fourth-quarter drives.

There's no reason to panic in Kansas City, but the Chiefs need the upcoming matchup with the New York Jets to be a get-right game. -- Moton

The Minnesota Vikings were perfect in the standings for the first two months of the season, but that ended on the first day of November. Despite their mediocre quarterback play, the Vikings are still one of the league's best teams, so they should remain within the top 10 in the power rankings for now.

However, Minnesota could start to tumble in the next few weeks. They'll face the Buffalo Bills, the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field, and the San Francisco 49ers. With Kyler Murray under center, the Vikings may struggle to keep pace with those teams.

Remember, when Minnesota beat Green Bay in Week 1, Carson Wentz came in and threw for three touchdowns. Murray has five touchdown passes in six games. -- Moton

Week 8 Result: Won vs. Indianapolis 42-7

The Jacksonville Jaguars dominated a down-and-out opponent in the Indianapolis Colts--which is exactly what Liam Coen's squad should do as the AFC South's best squad.

Bhayshul Tuten continues to blossom into a legitimate lead back. The second-year ball-carrier set career-highs Sunday with 104 rushing yards and 55 receiving yards. His increased usage can take pressure off of quarterback Trevor Lawrence. Case in point, Lawrence became the first quarterback since the 2015 season to throw for three touchdowns despite attempting fewer than 15 passes.

Through the rest of November, the Jaguars can run away with the division since they face a Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens, the Tennessee Titans (twice) and a JJ McCarthy-led New York Giants in the coming weeks. -- Sobleski

The Chicago Bears head into their second Monday Night Football game of the season on a three-game winning streak. This time, they're on the road against the Seattle Seahawks, who are coming off a dominant 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs.

If the Bears win, they'll be a half-game behind the NFC North-leading Minnesota Vikings, who took their first loss in Week 8. -- Moton

Week 8 Result: Won vs. Kansas City 28-24

The Denver Broncos avenged their season-opening blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, limiting running back Kenneth Walker III to 69 rushing yards after he had run for a career-high 173 yards in their previous meeting.

The Broncos conquered the AFC West's best team and moved to the top spot in the division. Although the other writers on this panel may not agree, Denver deserves a top-five spot in the power rankings because of its quality wins against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks, and Chiefs.

The Broncos have played through a tough schedule and have one of the league's best records, which speaks to their strong first-half run. -- Moton

The San Francisco 49ers have used the extra time around their bye to help retool their roster. The Niners are a legitimate contender, but injuries have once again played a significant role. So, general manager John Lynch continues to see what players might be available to pull off a trade.

San Francisco already acquired three-time Pro Bowler DeForest Buckner to join Nick Bosa, Osa Odighizuwa, Keion White, Mykel Williams and rookie Gracen Halton along the defensive front. Lynch may not stop there.

"San Francisco is still sniffing around for wide receiver help," the Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported .

Mike Evans has been banged up, while De'Zhaun Stribling and Ricky Pearsall are on injured reserve. San Francisco should be looking for another target so they won't be forced to rely on Deebo Samuel, Brandin Cooks and Christian Kirk down the stretch. -- Sobleski

Sunday's blowout win over the Ravens is at least a little misleading—Baltimore was forced to turn to an undrafted rookie quarterback after both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) went down. But elite teams win the games they are supposed to—and the Bills made short work of the undermanned Ravens.

It was a workmanlike effort. Buffalo wasn't great running the ball, averaging just 3.6 yards per carry. But James Cook topped 100 total yards, and both he and Josh Allen found the end zone. A much-maligned Bills defense didn't let the Ravens get anything going—Baltimore had under 150 total yards and turned it over three times.

That defense remains cause for concern, but Buffalo's schedule is manageable over the next few weeks—meetings with the Jets and Dolphins follow next week's trip to Minnesota.

The Bills are clearly the class of the AFC East, and a Week 12 meeting with the Kansas City Chiefs could set Buffalo on a path toward the AFC's No. 1 seed. – Davenport

articles.title: Baker Mayfield, Jesse Bates III Scuffle Video Goes Viral from Bucs' Win vs. Falcons
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield didn't complete a single pass—and only attempted three of them—during Sunday's 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons. But he did land one pretty massive block on Atlanta safety Jesse Bates III that resulted in a now-viral scrap on the sidelines.
articles.body:
Baker Mayfield didn't complete a single pass —and only attempted three of them—during Sunday's 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons. But he did land one pretty massive block on Atlanta safety Jesse Bates III that resulted in a now-viral scrap on the sidelines.

Mayfield didn't need to be much more than an occasional blocker during Sunday's win, with the Bucs rushing for 324 yards on offense and intercepting Michael Penix Jr. four times on defense.

Tampa Bay will probably need him to return to his regular-scheduled duties of actually throwing the football during next Sunday night's matchup against the Chicago Bears, however.

articles.title: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson breakup report sparks confusion as UNC staff unaware of alleged split
articles.summary: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson have reportedly ended their romantic relationship, but their public appearances together have made the news difficult to
articles.body: Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson have reportedly ended their romantic relationship, but their public appearances together have made the news difficult to understand. According to a report by TMZ published on October 30, the 74-year-old North Carolina head coach and his 25-year-old girlfriend quietly separated in late 2025. Neither has publicly confirmed the news. Even more surprising, USA Today reported that some UNC football staff members were unaware of the reported split, despite Hudson continuing to appear alongside Belichick.Their continued contact has made it harder to separate private developments from public appearances this season.Five public appearances by Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson kept their relationship in the spotlightThe reported timeline is particularly surprising because Hudson continued to support Belichick at several public events. Their appearances gave people little reason to believe that they had gone their separate ways.Here are five moments that added to the confusion.First, the two attended the Kentucky Derby in May 2026. They travelled together on a private jet and appeared comfortable in each other's company. Hudson also shared a picture of them holding hands at Churchill Downs on May 2. Her caption read, "Not the first time we've trudged through the mud together."Second, Hudson continued to appear at North Carolina football games. She was seen supporting Belichick from the sidelines during the 2026 season. Her presence at these games made the reported late-2025 split even harder for outsiders to understand.Third, the pair attended a UNC men's basketball game together. Their appearance showed that they were still spending time together outside the football field.Fourth, Belichick showed his support for Hudson at the US Worlds Trials cheer competition. Hudson later shared a selfie with him and referred to him as "Bill the WAG." The post was another public sign of their connection.Fifth, Belichick spoke about Hudson during a September interview with The Wall Street Journal. He pushed back against claims that she had been involved in running UNC's football program. His comments showed that he was still willing to address questions about her role in his professional life.However, these appearances do not confirm that the two were still romantically involved. They may have remained close because of their personal and business connections.Bill Belichick's private life and UNC role face fresh questions after Jordon Hudson split reportThe secrecy around the reported breakup has also brought attention back to Belichick's long history of keeping details away from the media.During his time with the New England Patriots, he rarely gave reporters much information beyond what he had to share. His short answers and limited comments often left questions unanswered. This approach followed him through some of the biggest moments of his coaching career.That included Spygate, when the Patriots were punished for recording opponents' defensive signals, and Deflategate, which involved underinflated footballs during the 2014 AFC Championship Game. His final years in New England also brought questions about the team's decline and Tom Brady's departure.At UNC, Belichick has faced questions about changes within his coaching staff. His son Steve left his position as defensive coordinator, while general manager Michael Lombardi also stepped down. The reported breakup has added another personal story to the attention surrounding his second season with the Tar Heels.However, there is an important detail that makes the breakup report less clear. On October 31, USA Today reported that two people inside the UNC football office, including a senior staff member, were unaware of the split. Meanwhile, WRAL reported on November 1 that people around the program had seen little evidence that the couple had separated. Sources who worked with Hudson also said they were unaware of a breakup.Neither Belichick nor Hudson has publicly confirmed the reported separation. TMZ has also said that the reason for the split and who ended the relationship remain unknown. Its sources claimed that the two remain close friends and are committed to their business partnerships. The outlet also reported that Hudson had started seeing other people.For Belichick, the bigger question is how his time at UNC will shape the way people remember his career. He has six Super Bowl wins as a head coach, but his post-Patriots years have brought a different kind of attention. His relationship with Hudson has often attracted as much public interest as his work on the football field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kyler Murray Injured, Latest Updates on Vikings QB's Hamstring, Status vs. Bills in NFL Week 9
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings got some bad news about their starting quarterback on Monday.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings got some bad news about their starting quarterback on Monday.

Coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters Kyler Murray came away from the 19-15 defeat to the Detroit Lions with a hamstring issue. The full extent of his injury isn't yet known.

Murray's tenure with the Vikings got off to a rough start in Week 1, as he was forced to exit against the Green Bay Packers in Minnesota's third offensive drive. He attempted to slide while scrambling and took a hard hit from Javon Bullard.

He was unable to return to the game and finished his first game as a Viking with just 18 passing yards, nine rushing yards and an interception.

Luckily for the Vikings, veteran quarterback Carson Wentz came in and threw for 133 yards and three touchdowns, helping Minnesota come back from a 12-point deficit to win 37-22 and start the season on the right note.

Murray is coming off an injury-filled 2025 campaign that saw him play just five games for the Arizona Cardinals as he finished the season with 962 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions.

He signed with the Vikings in March and later won the starting quarterback job, hoping to get a fresh start. Unfortunately for him, his season started with an injury, and his performance since returning has been inconsistent.

If Murray has to miss time, Wentz will presumably elevate into the starting role for Week 9 matchup with the Buffalo Bills.

articles.title: Lions say 'preliminary indications are positive' for linebacker Jack Campbell after neck injury
articles.summary: Jack Campbell's Detroit Lions said preliminary indications are positive after his neck injury, but key questions about mobility remain unanswered.
articles.body: There is good news for Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, per the team, but details of his condition and whether he has motion in his extremities remain scarce following Monday's latest update. The Lions on Monday announced "preliminary indications are positive" for Campbell's condition. But "out of respect for Jack and his family, we will not share further information at this time." "It's positive, you know?" coach Dan Campbell told reporters. "So your prayers are working. Please continue to do that." Campbell, no relation to Jack Campbell, went so far as to call his defensive captain's condition "a small setback." PACKERS WR CHRISTIAN WATSON GETS CHECKED AT HOSPITAL AFTER SCARY INJURY, SOMEHOW RETURNS TO LAMBEAU FIELD And while this is uplifting and paints a picture that the player's medical situation is trending in a good direction, it leaves a lot unclear. Specifically, no one has said whether Campbell has regained full or any mobility since he was removed from the Ford Field turf on Sunday on an immobility stretcher and cart. Despite the vague nature of the situation, Dan Campbell shared how he and several of the team's players visited Jack Campbell and his family at the hospital on Sunday evening. "I got to go see him last night. It was good. It was positive," Dan Campbell said. "… Got to see his parents, talk to his wife. And everybody's in good spirits. "And it's about the recovery and it's a small setback. That's the family. They're, you know, very positive." This was the third update on Campbell's status the Lions have delivered since the end of their game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Neither of the first two updates relieved concerns about whether Campbell had movement in his extremities, either. That message, if it is to come at all, will have to continue to wait, perhaps out of caution that what is finally reported remains true. Uncertainty was very much a worry to anyone who saw the play that led to Campbell's problem. Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson caught a pass in the middle of the field and was soon sandwiched by two Lions' defenders, including Campbell. The problem is Campbell arrived at the contact while falling to his knees and appeared to have his head slanted upward, so he made contact with his facemask rather than his shoulders and arms. Campbell immediately collapsed and lay motionless, his arms dropping to his side. On a positive note, Campbell did not require help breathing. The Lions are too familiar with neck and spinal cord injuries that derail NFL careers and change the direction of players' lives. Mike Utley’s career ended on Nov. 17, 1991, when the Lions guard fell forward and landed on his head while blocking against the Los Angeles Rams at the Pontiac Silverdome. Utley fractured the vertebrae in his neck and severely damaged his spinal cord. Utley was paralyzed from the chest down despite the fact he famously flashed a thumbs-up sign as he was taken from the field, a gesture that became a symbol of his determination. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Reggie Brown’s career ended on Dec. 21, 1997, when the Lions linebacker struck his head while making a tackle during a victory over the New York Jets. Brown eventually regained the ability to walk, but his was a life-threatening incident because he bruised his spinal cord and briefly stopped breathing. He received emergency resuscitation, neck surgery and extensive rehabilitation. Situations like this are seemingly impossible to forget. "That's difficult, you know, it's difficult," Dan Campbell said. "You don't ever want to see somebody like that on the field, but when you see Jack, Jack never lays on the field ever, no matter what it is. "And that's when you're like, it puts it in perspective … when you're in the world we're in, you know, you got to snap back, and it's not an easy thing to do."
