articles.title: Lions say LB Jack Campbell continues to recover in the hospital, early indications are positive
articles.summary: Campbell is Detroit's leading tackler this season.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions provided an update on linebacker Jack Campbell on Monday.

"Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital. Preliminary indications are positive, and out of respect for Jack and his family, we will not share further information at this time."

Lions head coach Dan Campbell (no relation) also spoke to the media on Monday and led with an update about the linebacker.

"It's positive. Your prayers are working; please continue to do that. We'll leave it at that. Just continue to pray for him, but it is positive news on Jack."

Campbell missed the end of the Lions' win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. He was involved in a multi-player tackle that left him injured.

Medical staff checked out the Detroit linebacker, and quickly called for a cart with a backboard. Campbell was surrounded by teammates and was taken off the field and transported to a local hospital.

Detroit went on to win 19-15 , handing the Vikings their first loss of the season. Postgame , Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the linebacker is "being taken care of" but had no additional information about his condition.

Campbell is in his fourth season in the league this fall. The former Iowa standout, whom the Lions selected with the No. 18 overall pick in 2023, recorded three total tackles in the win. He's up to 57 on the season.

The Lions are on a three-game win streak and are 5-2, second in the NFC North.

Detroit heads on the road in Week 9 to take on the Miami Dolphins before crossing the pond to face the New England Patriots in Week 10 in Munich, Germany.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk Hires New Agent to Aid NFL Return, Latest Rumors on 49ers Contract Status
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has hired Drew Rosenhaus as his new agent, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has hired Drew Rosenhaus as his new agent, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

NFL insider Jordan Schultz first reported Aiyuk's agent change is part of his effort to return to the league.

Given his reserve/left squad status from 2025, the veteran pass-catcher will have to formally file for reinstatement before he can suit back up again.

Aiyuk created an almost daily spectacle on social media as he unsuccessfully tried to engineer an offseason move away from the 49ers.

At one point in June, he said he fired his agent and hadn't had formal representation since November 2025. Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio followed up to say Ryan Williams was still listed as Aiyuk's agent of record.

The 28-year-old's relationship with San Francisco might be damaged beyond repair . Even after injuries hit the team's receiver room hard early into the season, coach Kyle Shanahan had a succinct response when asked about Aiyuk:

Setting aside all of the off-field drama over the summer, other teams will be weighing the fact Aiyuk hasn't appeared in an NFL game since October 2024. Two full years is a long time for a player to be sidelined.

Hiring an agent, especially one as prominent as Rosenhaus, represents a small step in the right direction. The timing also keeps the door open for San Francisco trading Aiyuk prior to the Nov. 10 deadline, though the clock is obviously ticking there.

articles.title: NFL: Detroit Lions' Jack Campbell remains in hospital after neck injury with 'preliminary indications positive'
articles.summary:
Jack Campbell was carted off the field during final quarter of the Detroit Lions' 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday; Campbell hit Vikings tight end 
T.J. Hockenson with a tackle; linebacker signed a contract extension with the Lions in May that takes him through 2030
articles.body:
Campbell was placed on a backboard and driven off the field early in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 victory and remains in hospital being monitored.

The 26-year-old was breathing when taken to the medical facility.

A Lions statement released on Monday read: "Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital.

"Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family, we will not share further information at this time."

Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving after hitting tight end T.J. Hockenson for his third tackle of the game.

Campbell was drafted by the Lions with an 18th overall pick in 2023 and in May of this year penned an extension until the end of the 2030 season.

He was an All-Pro last season after becoming the first player in seven years to have 150-plus tackles and at least five sacks and three forced fumbles.

Speaking about Jack Campbell, who was made a captain for the team this season, head coach Dan Campbell said: You get voted captain, ⁠that says a ton. He earned every bit of that.

"He's ⁠trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give ​you the shirt off his back. ​He's just all heart, man. All effort."

articles.title: Travis Kelce's business venture timeline: From Tru Kolors and New Heights to Garage Beer, sports investments and more
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has found ways to build his career beyond the NFL, with investments in sports teams, fashion, media and consumer brands.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has found ways to build his career beyond the NFL, with investments in sports teams, fashion, media and consumer brands. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has developed a business portfolio that includes his clothing company Tru Kolors, the popular New Heights podcast and Ohio-based Garage Beer. He has also invested in Formula 1, Six Flags and the Cleveland Guardians, while exploring new opportunities in college sports.How did Travis Kelce start his business journey with Tru Kolors and New Heights?Travis Kelce’s first major business move came in 2019 when he launched Tru Kolors, his own clothing and lifestyle brand. Fashion had been one of his interests since childhood, and he wanted to turn that passion into something beyond his football career. The brand focuses on sports-inspired clothing, casual wear and personal style. It also gave Kelce a chance to build a name in the fashion industry rather than depend only on his NFL earnings.The brand received another major opportunity in August 2025 when American Eagle introduced its AE x Tru Kolors collection. Kelce worked as the creative director and took part in the design process, including the selection of fabrics, colors and styles. The collection featured more than 90 pieces, bringing his personal fashion ideas to a much larger retail audience.However, fashion was not the only industry Kelce wanted to explore. In 2022, he joined his older brother Jason Kelce to launch the New Heights podcast. The two brothers began discussing football, NFL stories, sports personalities and their experiences both on and off the field. Their natural conversations and different personalities helped the show reach audiences beyond regular football fans.The podcast became one of the biggest parts of Travis’s business portfolio. On August 27, 2024, Amazon’s Wondery announced a three-year agreement to handle its distribution and advertising. The deal was widely reported by Variety to be worth more than $100 million. Under the agreement, Wondery received the rights to distribute and monetize the show’s audio and video episodes. Listeners also gained access to early and ad-free episodes through Wondery+.Another important step came in October 2023 when Kelce joined an investor group connected to Alpine F1 Team. The group included fellow NFL star Patrick Mahomes, golfer Rory McIlroy, boxer Anthony Joshua and other well-known athletes. The investment was led by Otro Capital, alongside RedBird Capital Partners and Maximum Effort Investments. The group had invested €200 million for a 24% stake in Alpine Racing. Kelce joined as one of its strategic investors, not as an individual controlling owner.Why did Travis Kelce invest in Garage Beer and Recover 180?One of Travis Kelce’s biggest business partnerships began in June 2024 when he and Jason Kelce became significant investors, owners and operators of Garage Beer, an independent light beer company based in Ohio.The partnership was important because the brothers were not simply lending their names to a product. According to Garage Beer’s June 12 announcement, both brothers planned to take part in several areas of the business, including brewing, distribution, sales, marketing and expansion into new markets.Their connection with the company also had a personal side. Both Travis and Jason played college football at the University of Cincinnati, and Garage Beer was originally created in Cincinnati. The brothers were already familiar with the region and wanted to work with a brand that had roots in their home state.Their involvement helped bring more attention to the company, but the business also continued working on its own expansion plans. In September 2025, Durational Capital Management made a strategic investment in Garage Beer, adding another financial partner to its growth plans.The latest major financial development came in October 2026. Tiger Finance announced that it had provided Garage Beer with a $20 million revolving credit facility. The funding is meant to support the company’s growth, help it enter additional markets and give it room to expand its product range. It is important to understand that this is a credit facility, not a $20 million investment made by Travis Kelce.Apart from the beer business, Kelce also entered the sports hydration market. On September 2, 2025, Recover 180 announced that he had joined the company as an investor and brand partner. Recover 180 sells organic sports drinks designed for hydration and recovery.This partnership added another consumer brand to his portfolio. While Garage Beer focuses on the beverage market, Recover 180 connects more closely with his experience as a professional athlete. His association with the company includes both a financial investment and a role in promoting the brand.What investments has Travis Kelce made in Six Flags and the Cleveland Guardians?Kelce’s interest in sports and entertainment investments continued in October 2025 when he joined an investor group connected to Six Flags Entertainment Corporation.The group was led by JANA Partners and also included business executives Glenn Murphy and Dave Habiger. According to the announcement released on October 21, 2025, the group collectively held an economic interest of approximately 9% in Six Flags.The investors wanted the company to improve its business performance, attract more visitors and offer a better experience to people visiting its amusement parks. Kelce also had a personal connection with the brand, as he had visited Six Flags parks while growing up.His role was part of a wider investment effort. He did not purchase the entire company or become its controlling owner. Instead, he joined other investors who wanted to work with the company’s leadership to improve its performance and create more value for shareholders.In May 2026, Kelce added another major sports investment when the Cleveland Guardians announced that he had joined their ownership group as a minority investor.The announcement came on May 27, 2026, and was especially meaningful because Kelce grew up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio. He has spoken about his childhood memories of attending baseball games in Cleveland with his family and friends. Becoming part of the Guardians’ ownership group gave him an opportunity to invest in a team that had been close to him since childhood.The Cleveland Guardians confirmed the news through an official announcement, while Kelce also discussed the investment on an episode of New Heights. He expressed his excitement about returning to his hometown in a new role and becoming part of the organization.Unlike his involvement with Garage Beer, where he and Jason have operational responsibilities, the Guardians investment is a minority ownership position. The club did not announce a specific ownership percentage or the amount Kelce invested.What is Travis Kelce’s latest business venture in 2026?Kelce’s business activities continued in August 2026 when Publicis Sports announced the launch of TEKTA in partnership with him and his representation firm, 3 Arts Sports.The venture focuses on name, image and likeness (NIL) opportunities in college sports. NIL rules allow college athletes in the United States to earn money through commercial deals involving their names, images and personal brands.TEKTA aims to help companies find suitable college athletes, create partnerships and measure the results of their marketing campaigns. This is an important area of business because brands are increasingly looking to work with college athletes and connect with younger sports audiences.Kelce joined the venture as an adviser, while 3 Arts Sports became its strategic operating partner. Publicis Sports brings its marketing experience and relationships with advertisers, while Kelce contributes his experience as a professional athlete with a strong commercial profile.The announcement was made on August 18, 2026, through an official Publicis Groupe press release. It also showed that Kelce was interested in business opportunities beyond traditional sports investments and consumer products.His involvement with TEKTA is different from his positions in Alpine F1, Six Flags and the Cleveland Guardians. He is not buying an ownership stake in a sports franchise through this venture. Instead, he is helping build a business that connects brands with college athletes.Garage Beer also remains an important part of his business activities, with the October 2026 credit facility providing the company with additional financial support for its expansion plans.From starting Tru Kolors in 2019 to entering the college sports marketing business in 2026, Kelce has developed interests across several industries. Some of his ventures involve active business roles, while others are minority investments or advisory partnerships.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Charley Hull dumps out SI swimsuit content from a boat, NFL player whiffs & college football's growing problem
articles.summary: Miami Dolphins rookie Chris Johnson's stunning sack whiff on Drake Maye left fans stunned, while college football attendance woes keep growing.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. How we doing, folks? Let's start this week — and this month — with a quick pulse check. Halloween is behind us. October is, sadly, behind us. We fell back yesterday morning. We're now less than 24 hours out from the midterms. Down here in Florida, it literally has not stopped raining since Saturday night. I've lived through dozens of hurricanes and millions of summer storms in my 30 years in the Sunshine State, and I've never seen anything quite like this. Just constant rain. Every road is flooded. My yard and the lake behind me are indistinguishable at this point. I have to use four-wheel drive to get down my dirt road, and even then, it's dicey. As for tomorrow's election ... So far today — and it's noon at the time of this writing — I've received 14 different texts and three calls. Some folks think Florida is turning blue. Others think we'll have this thing wrapped up by dinnertime. My official prediction, as OutKick's unofficial Florida guy: We'll stay red, but it won't be the landslide we've grown accustomed to. On a concerned scale of 1-10, I'm around a 4.6 right now. I was 0 in 2024, and 2 in 2022 for reference. Anyway, let's talk sports for a bit and leave all that other nonsense behind. Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where LPGA star Charley Hull starts Thanksgiving month on a boat in Ibiza. What a life! SPORTS ILLUSTRATED ADDS CHARLEY HULL TO ITS SWIMSUIT ROSTER, NASCAR'S NOSEDIVE & DO WE HAVE ANTHEM FATIGUE? What else? I've got the worst sack attempt you'll ever see out of Miami yesterday, a very clear attendance problem brewing in college football and wait till you see the ... reception ... the WNBA champs got in Golden State last night. I know I know — I said Friday I was done talking about anything non-Sophie Cunningham in the WNBA, but this is incredible. It's worth breaking the rule. Trust me. OK, grab you a sandwich for tomorrow's National Sandwich Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap! I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw this whiff Here's some free advice ... don't overlook Panera in the sandwich game. That's right. Panera. PANERA BREAD GRABS TOP HONORS FOR AMERICA'S HIGHEST-RATED FAST-FOOD BREAKFAST ITEM After two days of rain, I needed to get out of the house today. I couldn't take it anymore. So, I hopped in my boat and drove down the street to the Panera to work. I come here once in a while, mainly because the WiFi is better than most and I can get a cup of coffee for $2. Anyway, I've dabbled in lunch a few times over the past few months, and I gotta say — Panera sandwiches are top shelf. People like to give Panera crap for being too pricey or too corporate, and I usually agree with that crowd. But not here. They have a new French Ciabatta Dipper out right now that'll blow your mind. Not an ad, by the way (although I wouldn't mind if it was). Just figured I'd help everyone out on this first Monday of November. Good? Good! Now, let's get this week started with Miami Dolphins rookie corner Chris Johnson whiffing on a sack so badly yesterday, I thought my TV glitched. Seriously: What's going on with college football attendance? Goodness gracious. I've watched it 50 times and I still can't believe it's real. Heck, I watched it LIVE and seriously thought I was missing something. I saw him come around the end unblocked, and thought Drake Maye was about to die. At worst, it was going to be a sack. At best, I figured it'd be a strip-sack going the other way for a Dolphins touchdown. There was no scenario in which Johnson ... missed. Amazing. Now, to be fair, he's a rookie. He's also had a really good season, including a great play later in the drive that should've been fourth down stop, but the refs stink so they ruled it a first down. It wasn't, but that's neither here nor there. Regardless, it was an all-time whiff. I've watched football for 30 years. I don't recall seeing a whiff quite like that. Dolphins football in 2026, I reckon. Tank on! Next? I've said all year that I think college football has been a superior product to the NFL this season, and I still believe that. This upcoming Saturday is shaping up to be the greatest Saturday slate of all time. BUT ... as my old boss once told the entire company at a Christmas town hall before laying off half the office six months later, "I see some storm clouds on the horizon." Charley & welcome in the champs! Holy cow. I'm not going to share every post from that thread because I don't want to bog us down, but my goodness, it's ugly. Some of those empty stadiums are completely understandable. Maryland, for instance. The Terps stink, they just fired their coach, and they have no business being in the Big Ten. I get that one. Why in the world would anyone go to a Maryland game? But, it wasn't just the bad teams ... LOOK at the crowd for an actual ranked matchup between Texas Tech and Arizona: Or, for PENN STATE: Lordy. As I usually do on a Monday, I'd like to open this up for debate. What do you think is going on with college football attendance? TV ratings are good. The product on the field has been good. What's the deal? Me? I think the regular season has been watered down because of the playoffs, and I think — above all — folks have no real connection to these players anymore. These big programs don't have any more homegrown talent. It's all transfer portal kids. And they're all richer than most fans in attendance. The connection has been lost, and that connection is what made college football so great. Let me know! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com. OK, on the way out, let's all congratulate the WNBA champion Golden State Valkyries! I mean, it's just the perfect way to put a bow on this WNBA season. Listen to that crowd! They genuinely could not care less if they tried. Even the insufferable PA announcer is BEGGING them to get louder, and it's pointless. What a moment. What a season. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week, folks. Good start to the month. Let's all suffer through these next 48 hours together, and put this election in the rearview. On the way out, here's Charley Hull dumping out some SI Swimsuit content from a boat in Ibiza. Let's have a big week.

articles.title: Gardner Minshew Named Cardinals' Starting QB After Historic Comeback vs. Cowboys, Carson Beck QB2
articles.summary: After his outstanding performance in Sunday's historic comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys, Gardner Minshew II is getting a promotion.
articles.body:
After his outstanding performance in Sunday's historic comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys, Gardner Minshew II is getting a promotion.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur named Minshew the starter for this week's game against the Seattle Seahawks. Additionally, LaFleur said rookie quarterback Carson Beck will be Minshew's backup over Jacoby Brissett.

After Brissett struggled throughout the first half, the Cardinals brought in Minshew in the second half, and he completed 17 of his 23 passes for 188 yards and three touchdowns.

Arizona trailed 17-3 when Minshew came in, and he led a tremendous comeback, tying things in the final seconds when he connected with Michael Wilson. The Cardinals went on to win in overtime.

Brissett, who has started all eight games for the Cardinals, has thrown for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions this year. He had 119 yards and an interception on 10-of-23 passing when he came out of the game on Sunday.

Brissett's benching comes after the veteran quarterback signed a reworked deal in July that pays him $15.5 million for the 2026 season, with incentives that could move the total value to $21 million.

Minshew, meanwhile, is playing on a one-year, $5.75 million deal.

Minshew, a 2019 draft pick, has seldom been a starter in his career, much like Brissett. He was the QB1 in Jacksonville early in his career before bouncing around to a handful of different teams. He started 17 games with the Indianapolis Colts in 2023 before appearing in 10 games for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024.

Last year, he appeared in just four games with the Kansas City Chiefs.

Minshew is still just 30 years old and has the chance for a late-career revival. If he can match his performance from Sunday, he might be in for a big year.

Beck, a third-round pick out of Miami in the 2026 draft, could eventually be the Cardinals' solution under center, and the promotion to QB2 certainly makes his path to being the starter easier.

For now, he'll wait his turn behind Minshew.

Campbell, 26, sustained the injury during the Lions' game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

He was taken from the pitch on a stretcher after he hit his head while tackling tight end TJ Hockenson in the fourth quarter.

He received medical assistance before being removed from the field, having been lying face down on the ground.

"Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital," a Lions statement said.

"Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share any further information at this time."

The Lions won Sunday's game 19-15 when play resumed after Campbell's injury.

Campbell was drafted by the Lions with the number 18 overall pick in 2023 and signed a contract extension in May, through to the 2030 season.

articles.title: NFL Insider Floats Jacoby Brissett As Potential Ravens Trade Target Amid Lamar Jackson Injury
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are desperate for help in their quarterback room, and their solution could be the Arizona Cardinals' new emergency third-string quarterback.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are desperate for help in their quarterback room, and their solution could be the Arizona Cardinals' new emergency third-string quarterback.

The Cardinals named Gardner Minshew II their new starter on Monday and demoted Jacoby Brissett to the third-string behind Carson Beck. ESPN's Adam Schefter noted on NFL Live that the demotion raises "questions on his future there."

Schefter then floated Baltimore as a possible trade landing spot for Brissett after Lamar Jackson was placed on the injured reserve.

"We have an experienced, veteran starting quarterback who is now No. 3," Schefter said. "Any team that is out there, like a Baltimore, would certainly have to look at Arizona for a potential trade target."

On Sunday, Jackson returned to action after missing three games due to an ankle sprain, but he exited the matchup against the Buffalo Bills just a few plays into the game. Head coach Jesse Minter revealed after the game that the two-time MVP would need surgery on his thumb and would have to go on the injured reserve, meaning he'll miss at least four games.

Tyler Huntley, who filled in for Jackson when he was injured, came in momentarily but was also forced to exit because of a turf toe injury. He is expected to miss extended time as well.

The two injuries make undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano the starter heading into this week's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He completed 10 of his 21 pass attempts on Sunday for 91 yards and an interception in the 36-10 loss.

The Ravens also signed quarterback Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday. Reed, who went undrafted out of Western Kentucky in 2023, has not played in an NFL game but was with Baltimore during training camp.

Brissett has struggled to start the 2026 campaign, throwing for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He had 119 yards and an interception before being replaced by Minshew in the third quarter of Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.

It's unclear whether the Cardinals plan to move on from Brissett after benching him, but it wouldn't be surprising if the Ravens inquired about him before the trade deadline.

articles.title: "He's got a knife": Donna Kelce recalls terrifying Travis Kelce incident that could have ended badly
articles.summary: Last year, Donna Kelce gave fans a glimpse into the chaos of raising two future NFL stars, and her stories were anything but ordinary.
articles.body: Last year, Donna Kelce gave fans a glimpse into the chaos of raising two future NFL stars, and her stories were anything but ordinary. From a toddler figuring out how to start a car to a young boy throwing knives into the air, the Kelce household had its share of frightening moments. During an appearance on her daughter-in-law Kylie's podcast, Donna also settled a question many fans might have wondered about: Was Jason or Travis Kelce harder to raise? Her answer offered a funny but revealing look at how different her sons were as children.Donna Kelce explains why Jason and Travis were different childrenDuring her November 6, 2025, appearance on Kylie's Not Gonna Lie podcast, Donna Kelce opened up about raising Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce with her former husband, Ed Kelce.When Kylie asked which son was tougher to raise, Donna pointed towards the difference in their personalities. Jason, as the older child, was generally more willing to listen and follow instructions. Travis, on the other hand, had a habit of doing things his own way."You know, I think Jason, because he was the oldest and, you know, always the elder child in the family, not all the time, but especially with Jason, he would tend to listen and follow the rules," Donna explained. "Yeah. Travis isn't a rule follower."That difference became clear when Donna recalled an incident involving a three-year-old Travis. She had placed car keys and knives out of his reach, but the youngster found a way to climb up drawers and retrieve things.Donna remembered finding both boys inside the family car after Travis had managed to unlock it. He then put the key in the ignition and started the vehicle, sending it straight through the garage door."He knew exactly what we were doing," she said. "He knew how to unlock the car door, get into it, and then slam it shut. And I don't know how he did it, but somehow, and thank goodness, it was not an automatic. He put the keys in the car, he knew exactly what to do and turned it on and it jumped and went right through the garage door."Donna Kelce recalls a frightening childhood incident involving JasonTravis was not the only one who gave his mother a scare. Donna also shared a particularly alarming memory involving Jason and a set of knives.After returning home from picking Jason up at daycare, she heard someone shout, "Oh my God, he's got a knife!"She immediately knew which child was involved. Jason had apparently reached the knives stored high in a cabinet and started throwing them into the air while Travis watched."I knew who it was immediately," she said. "I knew it was Jason. He was the only one that was tall enough who could reach them."Donna rushed outside to stop him, later recalling how close the incident could have come to ending badly.Now a grandmother to Jason and Kylie's four daughters, Donna sees a striking difference between raising boys and girls. She said her granddaughters can sit down and enjoy crafts, something she rarely experienced with her sons.For Donna, those memories offer a glimpse of the energetic childhoods behind two of the NFL's biggest stars. And while both boys kept her on her toes, Travis clearly had a special talent for testing the rules.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Wayward 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk hires agent in first step toward possible NFL return
articles.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, estranged from a San Francisco 49ers team that holds his NFL rights, hired agent Drew Rosenhaus on Monday. The move could lead t...
articles.body:
After months of bizarre rants, followed by months of strange silence, Brandon Aiyuk has made his intentions clear: He wants back in the NFL.

The 28-year-old wide receiver, who has remained on the San Francisco 49ers ' reserve/left squad list since December, hired agent Drew Rosenhaus for representation on Monday, according to ESPN. Rosenhaus told ESPN he is "working on getting (Aiyuk) back to work and playing again in the NFL."

Aiyuk last played an NFL snap on Oct. 20, 2024, when he suffered a season-ending knee injury against the Kansas City Chiefs. Aiyuk was expected to make a full recovery and play again for the 49ers during the 2025 season.

A relationship that deteriorated over the course of multiple years reached a point of no return last season. Aiyuk is no longer welcomed in the team facility. General manager John Lynch said in January that his 2020 first-round pick would never again play a snap with the Niners.

The feeling is mutual. Aiyuk has made clear he does not want anything to do with Lynch, or head coach Kyle Shanahan , or anyone in the 49ers' organization, over the course of the past year.

"We is not cool. We won't be cool," Aiyuk said in an explosive June rant posted to his YouTube channel, with many expletives uttered to describe his disdain for Lynch and Shanahan.

Mentioning Aiyuk's name in the 49ers' building has become a forbidden act. The last time Shanahan spoke on the record about Aiyuk was Sept. 20, following a win over the Miami Dolphins. As wide receiver injuries began grow, he was asked if Aiyuk could be an option to provide some depth.

The days of Aiyuk running routes for Brock Purdy are long gone. In order for him to secure an NFL comeback, however, Aiyuk and his agent would need to do one more piece of official business with the 49ers, who still own his rights. San Francisco would need to release Aiyuk after he applies for reinstatement with the NFL. He would then be free to sign with another team.
